elements.quote: DESIGN AND SETTING: Rapid systematic review conducted in the medical school of the Federal University of São Paulo (SP), Brazil.
elements.reason: The abstract explicitly describes the work as a rapid systematic review.

elements.quote: OBJECTIVE: To assess whether patients undergoing pharmacological treatment for IMID present higher risk of worse outcomes when diagnosed with COVID-19.
elements.reason: The abstract provides an explicit objective.

elements.quote: METHODS: We searched CENTRAL, MEDLINE, EMBASE, LILACS, SCOPUS, Web of Science, L·OVE, ClinicalTrials.gov and WHO-ICTRP for studies evaluating patients diagnosed with COVID-19 who were undergoing pharmacological treatment for IMID.
elements.reason: The abstract states key inclusion elements (COVID-19 patients undergoing pharmacological treatment for IMID) but does not provide explicit main inclusion and exclusion criteria.
The abstract lists information sources but does not identify when each source was last searched.

elements.quote: Two authors selected studies, extracted data and assessed risk of bias and certainty of evidence, following the Cochrane recommendations.
elements.reason: The abstract indicates that risk of bias was assessed, but it does not specify the exact method/tool in the abstract (e.g., specific instrument).

The abstract provides results with odds ratios and confidence intervals but does not specify the methods used to present and synthesize the results (e.g., meta-analysis approach or qualitative synthesis description).

elements.quote: RESULTS: We identified 1,498 references, from which one cohort study was included.
elements.reason: The abstract reports the number of included studies (one cohort study) but does not report the total number of included participants or summarize participant quantities.

elements.quote: Those with RD seemed to have higher chances of hospitalization and mortality, but no statistical difference was detected between the groups: hospitalization: odds ratio (OR) 1.17; 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.6 to 2.29; mortality rate: OR 1.53; 95% CI 0.33 to 7.11 (very low certainty of evidence). Patients with RD were three times more likely to require admission to intensive care units (ICUs), with invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV), than those without RD: OR 3.72; 95% CI 1.35 to 10.26 (for both outcomes; very low certainty of evidence).
elements.reason: The abstract reports results for the main outcomes (hospitalization, mortality, ICU admission, and IMV) including effect estimates and confidence intervals.
The abstract does not state that a meta-analysis was conducted; it reports one cohort study included.

elements.quote: Those with RD seemed to have higher chances of hospitalization and mortality, but no statistical difference was detected between the groups
elements.reason: The abstract indicates direction of effect (higher chances with RD; ORs > 1) and compares RD vs without RD, but it does not explicitly state which group is favored.

elements.quote: (very low certainty of evidence).
elements.reason: The abstract reports limitations of the evidence in the form of very low certainty.

elements.quote: CONCLUSION: Patients undergoing pharmacological treatment for IMID seem to present higher chances of requiring admission to ICUs, with IMV. Additional high-quality studies are needed to analyze the effects of different treatments for IMID.
elements.reason: The abstract provides an interpretation of results and implications (need for additional high-quality studies).

elements.quote: Source of funding: None
elements.reason: The funding source is explicitly reported.

elements.quote: Our results are in line with those from a previous study that included 1,591 consecutive patients referred for ICU admission. That study showed that IMID was the most prevalent comorbidity in patients with laboratory confirmation as positive for SARS-CoV-2 who were admitted to ICUs. 6 The current systematic review also found one retrospective cohort study 28 suggesting that patients with IMID may be more likely to have worse evolution when infected by SARS-CoV-2.

elements.quote: Several limitations of the study that was included in the present review need to be highlighted. Lastly, no information on drug dose and duration of drug treatment was provided.

elements.quote: Therefore, we were unable to directly investigate the influence of each class of drugs on the course of COVID-19 in patients with IMID who were undergoing specific pharmacological treatments.

elements.quote:
Given that the current pandemic scenario has exposed shortages of professionals and resources, along with limitations to evidence-based clinical protocols, the outcomes of critical clinical importance would be those relating to the duration of usage of limited resources, such as the time taken to achieve clinical improvement, time to viral clearance and length of ICU stay.

The current evidence was assessed in the present review through methodological appraisal. Although this has provided scientifically rigorous data to inform further studies, the results reported here should be interpreted cautiously in analyses for decision-making processes.
elements.reason: Implications for clinical decision-making and evidence-based protocols are discussed, but explicit practice implications (e.g., concrete recommendations for clinicians/patients) are not clearly stated.

elements.quote:
We believe that there is a great need for prospective cohorts to be conducted in the future with the aim of examining representative samples of patients with IMID undergoing pharmacological treatments who are then diagnosed with COVID-19. Adjustments will need to be made for confounding variables such as in relation to use of multiple drugs, administration route, disease severity, comorbidities and age.

Through such studies, the level of confidence in the effect estimates can be improved.
